text: On 19 November 2024, a large number of people staged a demonstration rally organized by All Manipur United Clubs' Organisation (AMUCO), All Manipur Women's Voluntary Association (AMAWOVA), Manipuri Students' Federation (MSF) and Poirei Leimarol Meira Paibi Apunba Manipur with slogans from Kwakeithel to Keishampat in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) condemning the killing of 6 Meitei civilians (coded separately) and demanded the repeal of Armed Forces Special Powers Act (AFSPA) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Demonstrators engaged in a scuffle with police personnel and broke through barricades at Kwakeithel traffic point.

On 19 December 2024, MPs from the INDIA alliance (an alliance of opposition parties), including INC, staged a demonstration, raising slogans, at the parliament premises in the Delhi - Parliament Street area (New Delhi, Delhi) demanding an apology from the union home minister (BJP) - and called for his resignation - whom the demonstrators accused of making derogatory remarks against Dr. B. R. Ambedkar - who was a Dalit champion and played a key role in the drafting of the Indian Constitution. MPs from the NDA (an alliance of center-right to right-wing conservative parties), including the BJP, also staged a counter-demonstration at the parliament premises - demanding an apology from INC for insulting Dr. B. R. Ambedkar. The demonstrators scuffled with each other - resulting in head injuries to two BJP MPs. The INC president (MP) also claimed to have suffered injuries.

On 8 June 2025, locals from various localities including members of All Yairipok Meira Paibi Lup staged a demonstration on the first day of the 10 day total shutdown called by Arambai Tenggol across Manipur at Yairipok police station in Yairipok town (Thoubal, Manipur) against the arrest of 5 Arambai Tenggol members the previous day (coded separately) and demanded their unconditional release amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Police personnel fired tear gas shells and rubber bullets resulting in injuries to 2 women demonstrators. In response, demonstrators vandalized a police booth at Yairipok Bazar Traffic point and set it on fire.

On 9 July 2025, as part of the nationwide bandh (shutdown) under the banner of 10 central trade unions including the AITUC, CITU, INTUC, Hind Mazdoor Sabha (HMS), SKM and Self-Employed Women's Association (SEWA), people staged a demonstration in Muvattupuzha town (Ernakulam, Kerala) against the BJP-led NDA Union government over their new labor policies, push towards privatization and for not meeting workers' demands including fixing of minimum wage, legal guarantee for minimum support price (MSP) and regularization of jobs. The demonstrators pelted stones at a Kerala State bus to mark their demonstration. The police arrested two people.

On 9 July 2025, as part of the nationwide bandh (shutdown), demonstrators under the banner of 10 central trade unions including the AITUC, CITU, INTUC, Hind Mazdoor Sabha (HMS), SKM and Self-Employed Women's Association (SEWA) staged a demonstration at Govt LPS School in Aruvikkara village (Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala) against the BJP-led NDA Union government over their new labor policies, push towards privatization and for not meeting workers' demands including fixing of minimum wage, legal guarantee for minimum support price (MSP) and regularization of jobs. The demonstrators locked five teachers in a classroom who were later let out by the police.

On 9 July 2025, as part of the nationwide bandh (shutdown) under the banner of 10 central trade unions including the AITUC, CITU, INTUC, Hind Mazdoor Sabha (HMS), SKM and Self-Employed Women's Association (SEWA), people staged a demonstration in Guruvayur town (Thrissur, Kerala) against the BJP-led NDA Union government over their new labor policies, push towards privatization and for not meeting workers' demands including fixing of minimum wage, legal guarantee for minimum support price (MSP) and regularization of jobs. The demonstrators attacked an open hotel, a textile shop and a supermarket on Pattikkad-Peechi Road to mark their demonstration. The rioters assaulted a local TV crew.
On 15 May 2025, locals held a demonstration in Chauth Ka Barwara village (Sawai Madhopur, Rajasthan) over the death of a tractor trolley driver during their action against mining mafia.

On 27 July 2025, ABVP members held the college principal for eight hours and staged a demonstration at Veer Narmad South Gujarat University (VNSGU) in Surat city (Gujarat) after 3,400 call (offer) letters were sent to students against 135 vacant seats for BA first-year admissions.

On 4 December 2024, INC members, including the INC Leader of Opposition in the Parliament and an INC MP, staged a demonstration along the Delhi-Meerut Expressway at the Ghazipur border in the Delhi - Preet Vihar area (East Delhi, Delhi) after the police stopped them from traveling to Sambhal - where a demonstration on 24 November resulted in the death of 5 people (coded separately). Some people staged a demonstration and raised slogans against the INC leader, condemning the traffic chaos caused by the INC's demonstration - to which the INC members were suspected to have responded by assaulting the demonstrators.

On 1 April 2025, members of pro-Hindu organizations under the banner of Basanagouda Patil Yatnal Abhimanigala Balaga and the Kalaburagi Zilla Hindu Karyakartara Vedike along with members of Mashyal Mutt and Neelor (Hindu religious organization) staged a demonstration at Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Circle and later took out a march to the deputy commissioner's office in Gulbarga city (Kalaburagi, Karnataka) against the expulsion of a BJP MLA from the party for 6 years. The demonstrators raised slogans and burned tires to mark their demonstration.

On 3 June 2025, Senapati District Students' Association (SDSA), Mao Students Union (MSU), Maram Students Union (MKS), Poumai Naga Students Union (PNTM), Thangal Students Union (TAJ), and Zeliangrong Students Union staged a demonstration during the 48 hour picketing of government offices called by the All Naga Students Association, Manipur (ANSAM) in Senapati town (Manipur) against the BJP led central government's plan to fence the Indo-Myanmar border and the scrapping of Free Movement Regime (FMR), which would further separate Naga tribes on both sides of the border. Demonstrators overturned the Superintendent of Police (SP)'s car and vandalized his office following a confrontation after a CRPF personnel was ordered to load his weapon and threaten demonstrators.

On 23 November 2024, a large number of students of the University of Hyderabad staged a demonstration at the university administration building in Hyderabad city (Telangana) against a raid conducted by the chief warden, deputy wardens, and security staff on student hostel rooms. The demonstrators criticized the ongoing issues of poor basic amenities and infrastructure in the hostels and some students and officials sustained minor injuries.

On 9 July 2025, workers under the banner of 10 central trade unions including AITUC, CITU, INTUC, Hind Mazdoor Sabha (a labor group), SKM and Self-Employed Women's Association supported by LF held a demonstration as part of a nationwide strike by enforcing a shutdown of shops and businesses at Suri city (Birbhum district, WB) against privatization, price rise of essentials, unemployment, increase in contractual work and introduction of the 4 labor codes.

On 9 July 2025, workers under the banner of 10 central trade unions including AITUC, CITU, INTUC, Hind Mazdoor Sabha (a labor group), SKM and Self-Employed Women's Association supported by LF held a demonstration as part of a nationwide strike by enforcing a shutdown of shops and businesses at Chinsurah city (Hooghly district, WB) against privatization, price rise of essentials, unemployment, increase in contractual work and introduction of the 4 labor codes.

On 9 July 2025, workers under the banner of 10 central trade unions including AITUC, CITU, INTUC, Hind Mazdoor Sabha (a labor group), SKM and Self-Employed Women's Association supported by LF held a demonstration as part of a nationwide strike by enforcing a shutdown of shops and businesses at Alipurduar city (WB) against privatization, price rise of essentials, unemployment, increase in contractual work and introduction of the 4 labor codes.

On 27 May 2025, villagers (likely tribal based on geography) including Siang Indigenous Farmers Forum (SIFF) members staged a demonstration during Arunachal Pradesh Minister of Rural Development and Panchayati Raj's visit to Boleng town (Siang, Arunachal Pradesh) opposing the deployment of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) for the survey of the proposed Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP). Claims were made that it was a peaceful demonstration during which the minister elbowed a woman, while police assaulted another woman. The minister gave a conflicting account, stating that an enraged mob threw chilli powder at him and assaulted both him and his uncle, while personal security officers rescued them.

Around 14 February 2025 (as reported), villagers tied their sarpanch with a rope, displayed banners, held a 'ghagar morcha' (water pot demonstration), and marched to Pusad sub-divisional office (Yavatmal district, Maharashtra) over the failure of the sarpanch to address the water scarcity problem.

On 8 June 2025, Meira Paibi activists and locals staged demonstrations at several locations on the first day of the 10 day total shutdown called by Arambai Tenggol across Manipur, in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) against the arrest of 5 Arambai Tenggol members the previous day (coded separately) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Police personnel fired tear gas shells at Keishamthong, Uripok Polem Leikai, Naoremthong, and Lamboi Khongnangkhong areas to disperse the crowd and injured 3 demonstrators including a minor who sustained serious leg injuries. Along Tiddim road, demonstrators blocked roads at several locations including Hodam Leirak, Kwakeithel and Tiddim Ground following which police fired tear gas shells while demonstrators pelted stones and used slingshots. At Khagempalli, another group of demonstrators broke the windshield of a car carrying media persons while a motorcycle was set on fire at Kwakeithel.

On 19 February 2025, farmers and BKU members staged a demonstration, raised slogans, and burned sugarcane at the Collectorate in Bulandshahr city (Uttar Pradesh), demanding an increase in the price of sugarcane crops.

On 9 July 2025, CITU members holding a demonstration as part of a nationwide strike by workers under the banner of 10 central trade unions including AITUC, CITU, INTUC, Hind Mazdoor Sabha (a labor group), SKM and Self-Employed Women's Association supported by LF clashed with INTTUC members at Rampurhat city (Birbhum district, WB) against privatization, price rise of essentials, unemployment, increase in contractual work and introduction of the 4 labor codes.

On 17 May 2025, INC members, including MLA, burned effigies of the deputy Chief Minister, scuffled with police, and held a demonstration in Sardarpur town (Madhya Pradesh), against the deputy CM and Minister for Tribal Affairs for his objectionable remarks against a Muslim woman Army officer and spokesperson.

On 8 March 2025, thousands of Kuki-Zo women staged a demonstration and locked their arms together in an attempt to block vehicles including a Manipur State Transport (MST) bus escorted by security forces including police, Assam Rifles and BSF from entering the Kuki-Zo areas at Gamgiphai village (Kangpokpi, Manipur) opposing free movement in their areas following the resumption of inter-district movement, amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Security forces fired tear gas, rubber bullets, pellets, and live rounds at the crowd who pelted stones at them, resulting in the injuries to at least 30 demonstrators. The escorted MST bus managed to proceed towards Keithelmanbi (coded separately).

On 1 September 2025, locals from the Gujjar community held a demonstration and resisted the attempts by the police to arrest individuals involved in narcotics trade at Nadla village in Rajpura block area (Samba district, J&K). Police were able to detain one person involved in the narcotics trade while another escaped.

On 25 November 2024, Meira Paibi activists staged a sit in demonstration and blocked the road with boulders near MT gate of the Army camp in Leimakhong town (Kangpokpi, Manipur) condemning the abduction of a Meitei supervisor (coded separately) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.

On 1 September 2025, thousands of BJP members and supporters staged a massive demonstration in front of Rajiv Bhawan with slogans in Nagaon town (Assam) accusing INC of disrespecting the late mother of India's Prime Minister during the 'Voter Adhikar Yatra' (Voter Rights March) led by the Leader of the Opposition in Bihar and demanded an apology. Police personnel intervened between scuffling BJP and INC members resulting in several injuries to INC members.

On 10 December 2024, thousands of Panchmasali Lingayats community members led by a seer (spiritual leader) took out a demonstration march with anti-government slogans from Kondaskoppa village along Pune-Bengaluru national highway towards Suvarna Vidhana Soudha in Belagavi city (Belagavi, Karnataka) after the Chief Minister did not go to the Kondaskoppa demonstration site while the demonstrators demanded 2A reservation for the Panchamasali Lingayat community. Police personnel baton charged the crowd after demonstrators threw stones and footwear at them, detained several including a Panchmasali leader, BJP MLAs and an MP. Several vehicles belonging to officials and MLAs were damaged. Committee leaders claimed 20 injuries while police claimed 1.

On 29 October 2025, lawyers blocked Jaipur-Ajmer Road, set alight to decorations at a new court building and held a demonstration in Ajmer city (Rajasthan), over the lack of chambers and parking facilities in the new building.
